issues.legal_issue: A tenant’s surrender that does not satisfy the statutory formalities does not terminate the tenancy, and the tenant may seek restoration of possession under the statutory procedure for tenants.
material_facts: The tenant voluntarily handed over possession to the landlord, but the surrender was neither in writing nor verified through the required inquiry.
The landlord thereafter personally cultivated the land.
The tenant sought to recover possession from the landlord.
issues.conclusion: The surrender was invalid and did not terminate the tenancy. The tenant’s claim to possession arose under the Act, and the tenant could apply to the Mamlatdar under section 29(1) for restoration of possession.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 15, a surrender must be in writing and verified by the Mamlatdar; without those requirements it is not a valid surrender, so the tenancy continues and the landlord is not entitled to retain possession. Section 29(1) allows a tenant entitled to possession under the Act to apply to the Mamlatdar, whose functions under section 70(n) include putting a tenant in possession under the Act. The Court relied on Shankar Raoji v. Mahadu Govind (57 Bom. L.R. 65), Durgaben v. Bavla (58 Bom. L.R. 451), and Trambaklal v. Shankerbhai (62 Bom. L.R. 261).

issues.legal_issue: A tenant cannot use a summary eviction procedure when the Act provides a remedy before the Mamlatdar for recovery of possession following an invalid surrender.
material_facts: The tenant sought summary eviction of the landlord under section 84 after the tenant had voluntarily delivered possession under a surrender that did not comply with the statutory formalities.

The land was not land whose management had been assumed under the Act, and the case did not involve possession obtained through an invalid transfer or acquisition of the kind covered by section 84(a).
The tenant could seek restoration from the Mamlatdar under section 29(1).
issues.conclusion: Section 84 did not provide an alternative remedy in these circumstances; because the tenant had a remedy under section 29(1), the Collector had no jurisdiction to entertain the summary eviction application.
issues.legal_principle: Section 84 permits summary eviction in specified categories, including a person occupying land to whose use and occupation the person is not entitled where the Act does not provide for that person’s eviction. The present case fell only within section 84(c), whose condition that no other remedy be provided by the Act applied. The Court reasoned that allowing summary eviction despite the section 29(1) remedy would deprive the affected person of the appeal available under section 74 and allow the tenant to bypass the Mamlatdar’s inquiry. It considered Shankar Raoji v. Mahadu Govind (57 Bom. L.R. 65), Durgaben v. Bavla (58 Bom. L.R. 451), Trambaklal v. Shankerbhai (62 Bom. L.R. 261), Shankerlal v. Haria Vagha (Special Civil Application No. 8 of 1961, Gujarat High Court, 22 August 1961), and Krishna Mahar v. Hussain Miya (Special Civil Application No. 207 of 1956, Bombay High Court, 19 June 1956), finding them consistent with its interpretation.

rule.if: tenant_land_possession_case and tenant_applies_for_summary_eviction and surrender_lacks_required_formalities and statutory_restoration_remedy_exists and not land_management_assumed and not possession_from_invalid_transfer

predicates.tenant_land_possession_case: A person who held land as a tenant seeks to recover possession of that land.
predicates.tenant_applies_for_summary_eviction: The tenant applies to an administrative authority for summary eviction of the person possessing the land.
predicates.surrender_lacks_required_formalities: The tenant handed over possession under a surrender that did not satisfy the required writing and verification formalities.
predicates.statutory_restoration_remedy_exists: The tenant can apply to the designated tenancy authority for restoration of possession under the governing statute.
predicates.land_management_assumed: The land is one whose management has been assumed under the governing statute.
predicates.possession_from_invalid_transfer: The person’s possession was obtained through a transfer or acquisition invalid under the governing statute.

issues.definition: When a tenant seeks summary eviction after a formally invalid surrender, and a statutory restoration remedy exists without the case involving assumed land management or possession from an invalid transfer, the summary eviction procedure is unavailable.
